game: WAS@DAL Week 2 2026, kickoff 2026-09-20 16:25 ET, AT&T Stadium roof closed

script.base: Closing line is DAL -3.5 with a 51.5 total (nflverse games.csv), so implied totals are DAL 27.5 and WAS 24.0 in a closed roof. Base script is a competitive, play-heavy dome game that Dallas leads by about a score late: both sides throw because the total is high, Washington as the +3.5 dog throws to stay in range with Stefon Diggs (9 week-1 targets) as the hub, and Javonte Williams (12 carries week 1, Demercado 2) adds late clock-killing rushes. Week-1 defenses both leaked (DAL allowed 5.00 rush YPC; WAS allowed 6.00 rush YPC and 18.33 YPA in the middle), so the 51.5 is believable rather than a slog.
script.flip1: Dallas gets up big early, kills the clock, and Javonte's carries rise while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens yardage stall; Washington abandons the run, so Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 16-carry week-1 role shrinks and Diggs's targets spike.
script.flip2: Washington hangs or leads in a shootout: both passing games clear, Croskey-Merritt keeps carries, and Javonte never gets the late rushing script so his rush line dies while Lamb and Diggs both go over.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report, known before kickoff: DAL S Malik Hooker Out (forearm) and DAL LB DeMarvion Overshown Out (hamstring); WAS LB Frankie Luvu Out (groin), WAS TE Chig Okonkwo Out (hamstring), WAS DT Javon Kinlaw Questionable (back). Okonkwo played week 1 (3 targets, 16 yards, 39 air) and is out now, so John Bates (3 targets, 13 yards, 6 air) is the next TE up, with Diggs able to absorb leftover air yards. Hooker out helps WAS deep/intermediate options (Diggs 83 air, Antonio Williams 55 air, Terry McLaurin 22 air). Overshown out helps WAS tight ends, backs and short area (Bates, Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White). Luvu out helps DAL backs and tight ends (Javonte, Jake Ferguson 2/6, Brevyn Spann-Ford 2/14). If Kinlaw sits, Dallas's run game gains another interior edge; if he plays, that piece of the rush edge is gone. No inactives list (90-minute checkpoint not in pack). Sources: pack injury report and week-1 target lines only.

matchup.pressure: WAS EPA/dropback vs blitz was 0.66 vs 0.01 with no blitz, so Washington was better when Dallas blitzed, but Dallas only blitzed 27%. DAL EPA/dropback vs blitz was 0.87 vs 0.20 with no blitz, so Dallas thrived against pressure. That cuts the usual 'blitz forces checkdowns' path: Washington's 39% blitz is not a reason to fade Lamb/Pickens or to force a Javonte receiving over.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. The 6.00 YPC Washington allowed was one game against a different run game, Kinlaw played, and Dallas never led long enough to tack carries onto Javonte's 12, so 3.4 YPC on a pass-heavy 51.5 script left him at 41 or under. Lamb lost because flip 1 happened or because Pickens, who already had 104 air yards, took the one or two explosives Washington allows, and Lamb's 44 on 90 air was the real weekly band, not a matchup miss. The middle 18.33 YPA was three attempts. We also never saw a price, so the stand-in 41.5 and 44.5 may not have been the number anyone could bet.
slip_story: One story only: competitive dome game, Dallas up about a score, total near 51.5. Javonte rush over is the favorite-runs-late piece; Lamb rec over is the primary-target piece that still works if the lead stays inside a score. They conflict if it becomes a blowout, so this is not a clock-kill stack and not a shootout stack. Do not add a total under, a Croskey-Merritt rush over (needs Washington not to trail), a Diggs over (other script side), or a second Dallas WR. No TDs. Two legs max, and only if a real price appears; otherwise no slip.
